references.text: The prophecy that the Messiah's reign will continually grow: 'So his dominion shall be great and peace without end' ([ref:Jes 9:7|Isaiah 9:7]). This points to the fact that Christ must increase – his kingdom is to expand continually.

Malachi prophesies about the messenger who will prepare the way for the Lord ([ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1]). John the Baptist is this forerunner, whose role was temporary – to prepare the way so that Christ could appear.

John the Baptist testifies early on: 'He who comes after me has surpassed me because he was before me' ([ref:Joh 1:15|John 1:15]). John acknowledges Jesus' superiority from the very beginning of his ministry.

John says that among them stands one they do not know, 'he who comes after me, and for whom I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal' ([ref:Joh 1:26-27|John 1:26-27]). John emphasizes his subordinate role.

The context immediately before: The Baptist's disciples tell him that everyone is going to Jesus, and John responds by reminding them that he himself said: 'I am not the Messiah, but I have been sent ahead of him' ([ref:Joh 3:26-28|John 3:26-28]).

John uses the bridegroom metaphor: 'He who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice' ([ref:Joh 3:29|John 3:29]). This joy in making way is the immediate background for the words that Christ must increase.
The verse immediately after expands on this thought: 'He who comes from above is over all' ([ref:Joh 3:31|John 3:31]). Jesus' heavenly origin is the reason he must grow while John becomes less.

Jesus says that among those born of women, no one has arisen greater than John the Baptist, yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than him ([ref:Matt 11:11|Matthew 11:11]). This confirms that even the greatest prophet must make way for God's kingdom in Christ.
Christ must have first place in everything ([ref:Kol 1:18|Colossians 1:18]). Paul affirms the principle expressed by John the Baptist: Christ must increase and have supremacy over all.

God has exalted Jesus and given him the name above every name, so that at his name every knee should bow ([ref:Fil 2:9-11|Philippians 2:9-11]). Christ's growth and exaltation are God's will – the same confession made by John the Baptist.

Jesus is counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself ([ref:Heb 3:3|Hebrews 3:3]). Christ surpasses all forerunners, which reflects John's words that Jesus must increase.
